summary: Ernst Gombrich studied at the University of Vienna and worked in the fields of history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of London (1956–1959) and the Warburg Institute, where he served as research assistant (1936) and director (1959–1976).

An Indologist, Ernst Haas studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber (~1852–1855), the University of Bonn (~1855–1856), and the University of Tübingen (~1856–1859). He held positions at the British Museum (1866) and University College London (1875).
Ernst Haeckel studied at Frederick William University Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1857). He later served at the University of Jena (~1861–1909).

Working in Sinology and Buddhist studies, Ernst Johann Eitel studied at the University of Tübingen (MA ~1856–1860, PhD by 1871). He served at the London Missionary Society (~1865–1879) and as professor/lecturer at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1908).

An Indologist and linguist, Ernst Kuhn studied under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth, earning degrees from Tübingen and Halle-Wittenberg. He taught at Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, and Heidelberg, and served as professor at the University of Munich (1877–1917).

Ernst Leumann worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, studying under Albrecht Weber and completing degrees at Leipzig and Strasbourg. He worked on a dictionary at Oxford and held professorships at the University of Strasbourg and University of Freiburg.

Linguist Ernst Schwarz studied at the German University of Prague (~1914–1920) and the Deutsche wissenschaftliche Prüfungs-kommission in Prague (~1920). He held a post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1955–1963).

Working in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Ernst Steinkellner studied at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner. He served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1971) and as director at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Working in Indology and linguistics, Ernst Trumpp studied under Rudolf von Roth at Evangelisches Stift Tübingen (~1846–1850). He held posts at the East India Company (~1853–1854), the University of Tübingen (1871), and the University of Munich (~1874–1885).

Ernst Waldschmidt was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. After studying under Heinrich Lüders, August Hermann Francke, Albert Grünwedel, and Emil Sieg, he held the chair of Indology at the University of Göttingen (1936–1965).

Working in Indology and linguistics, Ernst Windisch earned his doctorate at the University of Leipzig under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Ritschl, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held chairs at Heidelberg, Strasbourg, and the University of Leipzig.
Ernst Zinn, working in linguistics and other fields, held academic posts at the University of Hamburg (~1947–1951), Saarland University (1951–1956), and the University of Tübingen (~1957–1978).

Erwin Rousselle specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies, earning doctorates at Heidelberg and habilitating at TU Darmstadt. He held professorships at Peking University and Tsinghua University, directed the Sino-Indian Institute, and held multiple appointments at Goethe University Frankfurt.
Working in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology, Esben Andreasen studied at the University of Copenhagen. In 1992, he served as a visiting researcher at Otani University.
Esei Sasaki worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as associate professor at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Eshin Nishimura studied at Hanazono University and Kyoto University (PhD). He served as president of Hanazono University (2002–2005) and director of the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (~1999–2004).
Esho Kawasaki worked in Buddhist studies. He served as director at Bukkyo University (attested 1999) and president of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).
Esho Mikogami was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who served as professor at Ryukoku University until 2003. He was also president of the Ryukoku Buddhist Society in 1997.

Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, Esho Yamaguchi studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1943). He held posts as professor at Osaka University (~1967–1982) and at Ritsumeikan University (~1982–1989).
Eshun Otsuka worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University and held a post there as a research student (attested 2013).
